introduction.text: The Arch of Septimius Severus is a white marble triumphal arch in Rome’s Roman Forum, built in 203 AD to celebrate Emperor Septimius Severus’ victories over the Parthians and to serve as a symbol of imperial power.

history.description: The Parthian campaign of 194–195 AD, which the arch commemorates.
The Parthian campaign of 197–199 AD, also commemorated by the arch.
The Arch was dedicated in 203 AD to honor Septimius Severus’ victories.
After Septimius Severus’ death, his sons Caracalla and Geta ruled jointly, but Geta was later assassinated by Caracalla, leading to the removal of Geta’s image from the arch.

design.description: The arch stands about 23 m high and 25 m wide, featuring a central archway flanked by two side archways, supported by composite columns on pedestals.

art.description: The arch’s relief panels depict the Parthian campaigns, winged Victories, the four seasons, and inscriptions praising the emperors.
